title: nucore-ai profile catalog
description: nucore-ai's own catalog-fetch wrapper (`GET /rest/profiles`) around the Dynamic Profiles object model -- the shape src/nucore/profile.py's `Profile.__parse_profile__` actually requires (`families[] -> instances[] -> {editors, nodedefs, linkdefs}`), and what src/unified/dev_tools/handlers/profile_authoring.py's validate_profile tool and its test fixtures (tests/unified/dev_tools/test_profile_authoring.py) actually exercise. This wrapper -- `families`/`instances`, per design/developers/nucore_domain_model.md §1/§12 -- is NOT part of the wire-format spec design/developers/plugin_model.md documents (see dynamic_profile_update.schema.json for that flat shape); it is nucore-ai's own concept for multiple family/instance catalogs merged into one document. Reuses the same defs/ object definitions as dynamic_profile_update.schema.json so the two 'views' of Dynamic Profiles never drift on NodeDef/Editor/Cmd/LinkDef field shapes.

family.description: src/nucore/profile.py's Family: `Family(id=f["id"], name=f.get("name", ""), instances=instances)` -- id is the only field the parser can't tolerate missing (`f["id"]` is a direct index, not `.get()`).

instance.description: src/nucore/profile.py's Instance: `Instance(id=i["id"], name=i["name"], ...)` -- both id and name are direct indexes (would raise if missing), unlike most other fields in this wrapper.
